Bins of an occasion covariate for stratified clip selection

Source: R/covariate_bins.R
covariate_bins.Rd

Cuts a continuous covariate of the occasions (an environmental gradient, such as the mean temperature of the night, or an acoustic index of the recording or minute) into bins that can stratify the draw of select_clips() (sampling_mode = "random_detections", argument covariates) and group the checks of stage 1 (precision_by_bin(), suggest_thresholds() and cell_status(), argument by).

Usage

covariate_bins(
  covariates,
  var,
  key = c("site", "night"),
  n_bins = 3,
  breaks = NULL,
  within = "site",
  name = paste0(var, "_bin")
)

Arguments

covariates

Data frame with the key columns and var, one row per occasion (or per night, when the covariate is nightly).

var

Name of the numeric column to cut.

key

Columns that identify a row of covariates and are matched against the occasions in select_clips(): any of site, night, recording_date, recording_hour, source_audio and occasion_id. night and recording_date are dates written as YYYYMMDD.

n_bins

Number of bins when breaks is NULL.

breaks

Optional numeric vector of breaks shared by all groups, instead of quantiles (bins are left-closed; the last one includes its upper end).

within

Columns within which quantile breaks are computed (NULL for quantiles over all rows). Ignored when breaks is given.

name

Name of the new column. Defaults to <var>_bin.

Value

The key columns (as character) and the bin, an ordered factor with levels q1, q2, ... (quantile bins, from low to high values of var) or the intervals of breaks. Rows with a missing var get a missing bin.

Details

The bins are computed on covariates, which should list every occasion (with or without predictions), so that the same bins serve the draw and every later table: the clip manifest and the validation tables keep their usual columns, and the same table returned here is joined to them by key (e.g. site and night) before the checks of stage 1. By default the breaks are quantiles within each site: acoustic indices depend on the gain and placement of each recorder, and quantiles over all sites would mix the covariate with the site.

A covariate used to stratify the draw does not depend on the score, so inclusion_prob stays exact. It may, however, be related to the verdict (an acoustic index rises when the species calls; the false-positive rate may change along a gradient). The calibration should then include the bin (e.g. tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | temp_bin)) or weight the clips by the inverse of inclusion_prob; see vignette("validation-effort").

Examples

nights <- data.frame(
  site  = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 6),
  night = rep(sprintf("202110%02d", 1:6), 2),
  temp  = c(18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20))
covariate_bins(nights, "temp", n_bins = 3)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 3
#>    site  night    temp_bin
#>    <chr> <chr>    <ord>   
#>  1 A     20211001 q1      
#>  2 A     20211002 q1      
#>  3 A     20211003 q2      
#>  4 A     20211004 q2      
#>  5 A     20211005 q3      
#>  6 A     20211006 q3      
#>  7 B     20211001 q1      
#>  8 B     20211002 q1      
#>  9 B     20211003 q2      
#> 10 B     20211004 q2      
#> 11 B     20211005 q3      
#> 12 B     20211006 q3      
covariate_bins(nights, "temp", breaks = c(15, 20, 25, 30))
#>    site    night temp_bin
#> 1     A 20211001  [15,20)
#> 2     A 20211002  [20,25)
#> 3     A 20211003  [20,25)
#> 4     A 20211004  [20,25)
#> 5     A 20211005  [25,30]
#> 6     A 20211006  [25,30]
#> 7     B 20211001  [15,20)
#> 8     B 20211002  [15,20)
#> 9     B 20211003  [15,20)
#> 10    B 20211004  [15,20)
#> 11    B 20211005  [15,20)
#> 12    B 20211006  [20,25)
